newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul won ends flat, weak long-term outlook holds.
newsitem.headline: Seoul won ends flat, weak long-term outlook holds.

text.p: The South Korean won ended Friday at its opening level as players who felt the market was overly heavy with dollars mixed with those who feared the won would fall again due to poor fundamentals, traders said.
The won ended flat at 849.00. It moved in a range of 848.20 to 849.10.
"If we look simply at the market positions, the dollar will weaken," said a Chase Manhattan Bank dealer. "But fundamentals such as rising trade deficit are towards a strong dollar."
The trade ministry has said strikes could push the trade deficit to a historical high of $3.9 billion this month.

Hans Kim, chief dealer at Banque Nationale de Paris, said the won was in a rebound because it fell too sharply over the past two weeks. "But in the long-term, the dollar has to strengthen, since we're expecting a historically high trade deficit," he said.
Major export industries have been hit by nationwide strikes in protest at the passage of a controversial labour law.
Dealers said they expected the won to move in a 848.50-849.70 range on Monday. The base mid-rate for Monday is seen at 848.80, against Friday's 849.00.
